request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rolling over a fiscal year now also soft-closes every period of that year that is still open. All 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

The change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/RolloverService.java`, and it's server-only; the front end didn't need anything new. After writing the `ROLLOVER` line, the rollover goes through the old year's periods in start-date order. Each one that is neither closed nor already soft-closed gets soft-closed through the same code path as a normal soft close, so it writes a matching `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED ... period=<name> total=<x>` line. Periods that were already closed, like 2026-11 in the test, are skipped. Everything happens in the same transaction as the rollover itself. I also updated the class's doc comment to describe this.

One decision for you: undoing a rollover does not reopen the periods it soft-closed, because the request didn't mention undo. If an undo should restore them, that would be a separate change.
